release_coverage_check.method:
Two independent checks, cross-validated against each other.
(1) FILE LISTING: enumerated every file at each published tag via the Hugging Face tree API with pagination, and matched video basenames against the video IDs in the authors' released stage-1 proposal.json. Matching covered both continuous/videos/sequences/ and continuous/videos/words/. Every unmatched ID was then substring-searched across all 6,700 repository paths to rule out a rename, a different extension, or relocation to another directory; all returned zero hits, while control IDs known to be present returned exactly one hit each under the identical naming convention.
(2) ANNOTATION INDEX: downloaded the dataset's own annotations.toml (sha256 dbe43236eca227ed8b77f7da13a3cdbd6e291434ec8ae3c4fcca95162b2c25c4, 770,281 bytes, 1,302 annotated video IDs) and matched the same proposal.json IDs against its TOML table keys. This check does not depend on filenames or directory layout at all.
The two methods agree on every video they both cover. The annotation index is additionally stricter: kamakura_019_202310_t001 has an .mp4 file but no entry in annotations.toml, so it has no ground-truth segments and cannot be scored. 'Usable' below therefore means a video file AND an annotation entry.
release_coverage_check.conclusion: No published release contains the paper's evaluation split. Of the 24 test videos the paper reports, only 19 are usable in the current release: four (kankoku_019_202310_t001, tsurukawa_018_202310_t001, tsurukawa_019_202310_t001, yokosuka_019_202310_t001) have no video file under any name in any tag, and a fifth (kamakura_019_202310_t001) has a video file but no entry in annotations.toml, so it carries no ground-truth segments to score against. Training coverage is worse: 151 usable of the 235 videos the authors' own proposal.json enumerates, against the 240 the paper reports. Six participant IDs the paper used (001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009) appear in no release, while the release adds participants 023-026 that postdate the paper. The paper's Section 3.2 consent statement explains part of the training shortfall but does not account for the missing held-out Dataset A evaluation videos.
release_coverage_check.consequence: Table 2 cannot be reproduced on its reported split from any public release. Evaluating on the obtainable 20 of 24 test videos would change the evaluation set, making any resulting mAP a different measurement rather than a reproduction of the published number, regardless of how close it landed.

split_terminology.issue: The paper and the code use different words for the same 24 videos, and the paper never uses the word 'test' for a data split at all. This record previously wrote 'test split', which imported the code's vocabulary into a description of the paper. The underlying set of 24 video IDs is unchanged; only the label is corrected.
split_terminology.paper: Section 5.1 is the paper's only statement: 'Of these, 24 untrimmed videos from Dataset A were held out for validation. The remaining 240 untrimmed videos ... were used for training.' The paper defines exactly two partitions, training and validation, and reports Table 2 on the 24-video held-out partition it calls VALIDATION. A search of the full text finds no occurrence of 'test', 'testing' or 'test set' as a data split.
split_terminology.code: hrpro/main.py and hrpro/dataset.py call the held-out partition 'test': they construct dataset(args, phase='test') and read split_test.txt. hrpro/log.py then maps that phase name onto the subset string written in gt_full.json via mapping_subset = {'ub-moji': {'train': 'Validation', 'test': 'Test'}}, and hrpro/eval/eval_detection.py keeps only annotations whose v['subset'] equals that string. Note also that the eval classes default to subset='validation' and that HR-Pro's upstream THUMOS14 convention, preserved in the same mapping, evaluates the 'train' phase against the 'Validation' subset.
split_terminology.resolution: There is one held-out partition of 24 Dataset A videos, not two. The paper calls it validation; the code's phase name for it is 'test' and it is loaded from split_test.txt. There is no third, separate test set anywhere in the paper, the code, or the released artifacts. Because the checkpoint-selection rule in hrpro/main.py saves the best model by mAP measured on this same partition, the paper both selects on and reports on it. That is the published protocol and is preserved here as-is, but it means the reported Table 2 numbers are best-epoch scores on the selection set, with no separate untouched test set held back.
split_terminology.usage_in_this_record: For precision, this record now says 'held-out split (paper: validation; code phase: test, split_test.txt)' where the distinction matters. The 24 video IDs, and every coverage count reported here, are unaffected by the naming.

public_availability_assessment.question: Is ub-MOJI a public dataset, and is the paper's data public?
public_availability_assessment.two_distinct_answers: These are different questions with different answers, and conflating them would misreport the paper. ub-MOJI IS a real public dataset: on main/v26.09 it publishes 1,297 continuous videos, 1,272 of them annotated, plus an isolated subset, under a click-through academic-research licence that this study has now accepted. It is genuinely usable for new research. What is NOT public is the specific data this paper ran on.

paper_data_coverage.detail: Only 65.6% of the videos the paper's own splits enumerate are obtainable from any public release.

signer_coverage.detail: Six of the paper's eighteen signers have no video anywhere in any release. The release separately contains four signers (023-026) that postdate the paper and were never part of its experiments, so the release is not a superset of the paper's data despite being larger overall.

public_availability_assessment.discrepancy_with_the_papers_own_account: The paper's Section 3.2 says Dataset B comprised 17 signers over two sessions and that 'only data from Session 2 (13 signers) is made public', which implies 4 withheld signers. Six of the paper's signers are in fact absent. The consent statement therefore does not fully account for the observed absence even at signer granularity, and it does not address the 38 video-level gaps inside signers that ARE present, including 5 videos of the held-out partition.
public_availability_assessment.characterisation: For reporting purposes: the artifact is a public dataset, but the paper's experiment is not reproducible from it. Roughly a third of the paper's videos, a third of its signers, and a fifth of its held-out evaluation partition are unavailable at every published version. The correct statement is not 'the dataset is private' but 'the released dataset is not the dataset the paper used'.

metric_definitions.name: mean Average Precision at a temporal IoU threshold (mAP@tIoU)
metric_definitions.implementation: hrpro/eval/eval_detection.py in source published-code, a fork of the ActivityNet-style detection evaluation used by upstream HR-Pro. Average Precision is computed per syllable class from predicted temporal segments matched to ground-truth segments at a given tIoU threshold, then averaged over the 46 syllable classes listed in hrpro/options.py.
metric_definitions.version: As pinned at ub-hrpro b660ca9c72fb31a0208f7525dc023e6acdb59b6e; the repository declares no separate evaluation-package version.
metric_definitions.aggregation: Per-threshold values are the mean AP over the 46 classes at that single tIoU threshold. The three range columns are the arithmetic mean of the per-threshold mAP values over the thresholds in the range, on the grid np.linspace(0.1, 0.7, 7) declared in hrpro/cfgs/ub-moji_hyp.yaml: (0.1:0.5) averages 5 thresholds, (0.3:0.7) averages 5, and (0.1:0.7) averages all 7.
metric_definitions.unit_or_scale: percent, 0-100, reported to one decimal place
metric_definitions.paper_evidence: Table 2 caption, page 6: 'Detection performance (mAP %) at multiple tIoU thresholds and their averaged values using different input encoders.' Section 5.1: 'using mean Average Precision (mAP) across multiple Temporal Intersection over Union (tIoU) thresholds ranging from 0.1 to 0.7.'

experiments.system: I3D (RGB + Optical Flow) encoder feeding two-stage HR-Pro. Baseline row: 2048-dimensional I3D features, no joint angles, no contrastive pretraining.
experiments.checkpoint_rule: HR-Pro selects the checkpoint by best test mAP during training: hrpro/main.py saves model1_seed_{seed}.pkl in stage 1 and model2_seed_{seed}.pkl in stage 2 whenever the periodic evaluation exceeds the running best. Stage 1 evaluates every test_iter=50 steps over 5000 steps; stage 2 evaluates every test_epoch=1 over max_epochs=20. Reported values come from the stage-2 model. This rule selects on the same 24-video partition that is reported. The paper calls this partition 'validation' (Section 5.1) and never defines a separate test set; the code's phase name for it is 'test' (split_test.txt), mapped to the gt_full.json subset string 'Test' by hrpro/log.py. Selection and reporting therefore happen on one and the same held-out partition.
experiments.paper_evidence: Table 2 row 'I3D (RGB, Optical Flow)', page 6. Section 5.2 item 1: 'I3D (RGB + Flow): Baseline model using 3D ConvNet features'. feature_dim 2048 is documented in the comment in hrpro/cfgs/ub-moji_hyp.yaml.
experiments.protocol: Two-stage HR-Pro per Section 5.1: stage 1 is 5000 steps, batch size 8, lr 1e-4; stage 2 is 20 epochs, batch size 10, lr 5e-5. Section 5.1 states 8 attention heads are used when joint angle features are excluded. Features come from the pinned video-features-submodule I3D extractor.

experiments.system: I3D (RGB + Optical Flow) concatenated with 20-dimensional MediaPipe joint-angle features, feeding two-stage HR-Pro.
experiments.checkpoint_rule: Same best-test-mAP rule as experiment i3d, applied to this configuration's stage-2 model.
experiments.paper_evidence: Table 2 row 'I3D (RGB, Optical Flow) + Angular', page 6. Section 5.2 item 2: 'I3D + Angular: I3D baseline augmented with joint angle features'. Section 6: 'joint angle features, which led to over 30% improvement in the I3D configuration'.
experiments.protocol: As experiment i3d, except that Section 5.1 specifies 2 attention heads when joint angle features are included: 'The number of attention heads in the multi-head module was adapted to the input dimensionality: 8 heads were used when joint angle features were excluded, and 2 heads were used when they were included.' Angle features come from feature_extraction/angle_features with a MediaPipe hand_landmarker.task model.

experiments.system: VideoMAE v2 (RGB only) encoder feeding two-stage HR-Pro; 768-dimensional features, no contrastive pretraining, no joint angles.
experiments.checkpoint_rule: Same best-test-mAP rule as experiment i3d, applied to this configuration's stage-2 model.
experiments.paper_evidence: Table 2 row 'VideoMAE v2 (RGB)', page 6. Section 5.2 item 3: 'VideoMAE v2 (RGB): Transformer-based encoder without Flow or angles'.
experiments.protocol: As experiment i3d with 8 attention heads and feature_dim 768. This matches the committed hrpro/cfgs/ub-moji_hyp.yaml defaults (backbone videoMAE, feature_dim 768, RAB_args num_heads 8) and the authors' released stage-1 config.json.

experiments.system: VideoMAE v2 (RGB) with SimCLR-style point-supervised contrastive pretraining, feeding two-stage HR-Pro. The paper's best configuration at tIoU 0.1-0.5.
experiments.checkpoint_rule: Two selection points. The contrastive-pretraining stage (videomae/main.py) runs the epochs given on its command line; videomae/README.md shows --epochs 30, while the paper's Section 5.1 does not state an epoch count or a pretraining checkpoint-selection rule. The downstream HR-Pro stage then uses the same best-test-mAP rule as experiment i3d.
experiments.paper_evidence: Table 2 row 'VideoMAE v2 (RGB) + Point-Sup. CL', page 6. Section 5.2 item 4: 'VideoMAE v2 + Point-Sup. CL: With contrastive pretraining based on point annotations'. Abstract: 'Our top model achieves up to 93.4% mAP at tIoU 0.1-0.5'.
experiments.protocol: Section 5.1: Gaussian kernel with sigma=4 frames for temporal sampling; memory bank of 65,536 entries; encoder initialized from a ViT-Base model pretrained on Kinetics (videomae/README.md identifies vit_b_k710_dl_from_giant.pth from VideoMAE v2, distilled from ViT-G on Kinetics-710); Schedule-Free RAdam at lr 1e-4; InfoNCE temperature tau=0.1; projection head 768 -> 1024 -> 512 (Figure 3). Downstream HR-Pro as experiment videomae with 8 heads.

experiments.system: VideoMAE v2 (RGB) with point-supervised contrastive pretraining concatenated with 20-dimensional MediaPipe joint-angle features, feeding two-stage HR-Pro. The paper's full model.
experiments.checkpoint_rule: Same two selection points as experiment videomae-cl, with the downstream best-test-mAP rule applied to this configuration's stage-2 model.
experiments.paper_evidence: Table 2 row 'VideoMAE v2 (RGB) + Point-Sup. CL + Angular', page 6. Section 5.2 item 5: 'VideoMAE v2 + Point-Sup. CL + Angular: A model combining all components'.
experiments.protocol: As experiment videomae-cl, except 2 attention heads per the Section 5.1 head-count rule for configurations that include joint angle features.

reason.detail: Producing this number requires the ub-MOJI videos on the paper's reported splits. Dataset access was granted on 2026-09-24, removing the access barrier, but two independent checks then showed that no public release contains those splits. Only 19 of the 24 reported evaluation videos are usable: four have no video file in any of the four published tags, and a fifth has a file but no entry in the dataset's own annotations.toml. Training coverage is 151 usable of the 235 IDs in the authors' proposal.json, against 240 reported. Evaluating on the usable subset would change the evaluation set and yield a different measurement rather than this published value.

evidence: File enumeration across all four tags against the 259 IDs in the authors' released proposal.json: best coverage 172/259 (v26.09/main); 20/24 test IDs have a video file at every tag. Unmatched IDs return zero substring hits across all 6,700 paths while present controls return exactly one, ruling out renames.

The dataset's own annotations.toml (sha256 dbe43236eca227ed8b77f7da13a3cdbd6e291434ec8ae3c4fcca95162b2c25c4, 1,302 IDs), checked independently of filenames, contains 19 of the 24 test IDs; it flags the same four missing videos plus kamakura_019_202310_t001, which has a file but no ground-truth segments.
Test videos with no file in any tag: kankoku_019_202310_t001, tsurukawa_018_202310_t001, tsurukawa_019_202310_t001, yokosuka_019_202310_t001.
Paper Section 3.2, Dataset B: 'While our model was trained on data from both sessions, only data from Session 2 (13 signers) is made public due to participant consent agreements.'
